task.description:
Investigate GH #600 (ISS-0629, MAJOR label but MINOR actual severity per the issue's own text -- watchdog mechanism itself is not defective, this is a test-assertion timing margin issue): TC-LUA-10-03 in src/lua/limiter_wiring_test.zig intermittently fails under system load (observed 3 fail / 2 pass across 5 consecutive runs, zero code changes between runs).

ORCH already independently observed this exact flake during GH-595's TEST-RUNNER pass (2 of 3 zig build test-lua runs showed 90/91 with TC-LUA-10-03 as the sole failure, 1 run showed 91/91 clean) and has already read the test source (src/lua/limiter_wiring_test.zig ~L575-600): the test runs a 200,000,000-iteration Lua loop via a raw lua_pcall, measures elapsed_ms via wall-clock timing (always exceeds the 1-second watchdog deadline by design), then IMMEDIATELY asserts watchdog_state.hasFired() with no retry/backoff. The watchdog thread (src/lua/timeout.zig, WatchdogState/WatchdogHandle, wired in GH-495/PR#593 earlier this session) polls the deadline on its own separate std.Thread every ~10ms (POLL_INTERVAL_NS) -- if the main test thread's assertion happens to run in the narrow window before the watchdog thread's last poll iteration actually flips its atomic 'fired' flag (a real, if narrow, race under OS scheduling pressure), the assertion sees false and the test fails, even though the deadline genuinely passed and the watchdog would have fired within another ~10ms.

The issue's own acceptance criteria offer two options: (a) 20+ consecutive clean runs (statistically implausible to guarantee given the root cause is a genuine race, not a fluke), or (b) restructure the test to poll hasFired() with a bounded retry/backoff instead of asserting immediately. Option (b) is clearly the right engineering fix -- confirm this yourself rather than assuming, and produce a precise diagnosis of exactly where the retry loop needs to go and what bound is appropriate (the watchdog's own poll interval is ~10ms; a bound of e.g. 500ms-1s with periodic checks would comfortably absorb realistic scheduling jitter without meaningfully slowing the test suite or masking a genuine watchdog failure, since a watchdog that NEVER fires within a full second after its 1s deadline already passed would still correctly fail the test).

This is a TEST-ONLY fix -- no production code in timeout.zig or limiter_wiring_test.zig's actual watchdog wiring needs to change, only the test's own assertion timing. Route to CODE-DESIGNER per the standard WF-03 pipeline (even though the fix is small, ORCH is following the standard pipeline steps rather than skipping the design gate).
acceptance_criteria: Root cause confirmed against real source (race between watchdog poll thread and immediate assertion)
Precise diagnosis of exactly where/how a bounded retry-with-backoff should replace the immediate assertion
Retry bound chosen and justified (comfortably absorbs scheduling jitter without masking a genuine failure)
Confirmed test-only fix, no production watchdog code needs to change
Routed to CODE-DESIGNER, not implemented directly
